topology: Two clients reach R1 through distinct physical input ports. R1 Loopback0 is the control-plane test destination; the remote HTTP server is reached through R1 and R2 using prepared single-area OSPF. Addresses, host gateways, SSH and server HTTP are prepared; the learner configures R1 CoPP.
implemented: Sixth ENCOR Security lab and38 ENCOR entries. Other-section counts and original CCNA ACL/AAA labs remain available. Permalinks retain the current site domain, path and query.

Two named IPv4 ACLs and match-any class maps classify OSPF and ICMP echo. COPP-IN orders the routing class, ICMP class and class-default; its only policer is single-rate two-color ICMP policing at8000 bit/s with1500-byte committed burst, conform/transmit and exceed/drop.

Only R1 aggregate control-plane input is attached. Router-bound echo is policed while transit server traffic bypasses CoPP. Separate physical ingress ports use the same aggregate meter, including a native simultaneous-client test proving that the clients do not get independent buckets.

Three small conforming echoes, complete12-request large probe groups with both actual replies and silent exceeded drops, independent PC2 traffic and real color counters prove operational policing. Windows1400-byte payloads produce1428-byte IPv4 datagrams; each source probe group retains its actual packet IDs.

Actual OSPF packet admission, Full adjacency and learned forward/return routes remain healthy. Authenticated SSH uses the permitted default class; the test runs a remote OSPF route query and logs out. Both client/server echo paths and complete remote HTTP200 delivery prove transit forwarding.

Five troubleshooting observations exercise classifier ACL deny fallthrough, wrong classifier protocol, physical input placement affecting transit, a one-byte committed burst that cannot admit a normal echo, and an intact but unbound policy. Required repairs need new correctly delivered/policed traffic after the incident.

ACL deny is a classification exclusion, not an interface packet drop. The intended fallback class transmits all12 real requests; the exact final classifier must still be restored for live configuration/save goals.

Bounded QoS decision evidence records actual aggregate control-plane and physical input-policer outcomes. It retains packet/probe/transaction IDs, actual actions and colors, policer settings and small classifier snapshots; histories cap at1000 rows, eight classes and eight entries per classifier, flag truncation and omit free-form ACL remarks. Cumulative counters remain separate and classifier/query calls alone cannot fabricate packet credit.

Question-mark help and Tab now expose the implemented show policy-map control-plane path and inline police rate/burst/color actions. Policy output includes actual ACL classifier matches and class-default Match:any, with no fabricated five-minute rates.

Practice starts0/16. Completed reference has four live configuration/save goals and no invented traffic or fault achievements. All16 earned observations survive YAML while operational meters, sessions and counters rebuild. Final save requires exact restored classifier/policy/attachment, R1/R2 startup equality, healthy addressing/gateways, OSPF routes, SSH/HTTP and closed management sessions.
scope: IOS IPv4 aggregate input CoPP lab. Existing packet classification and token-bucket forwarding semantics are preserved; changes add lab content, graded observations, bounded evidence, CLI help/completion and match display.
Routing and default classes deliberately pass their traffic; this exercise targets ICMP policing and is not a complete production hardening policy.
CPU utilization, hardware punt queues, distributed/output CoPP, NX-OS system CoPP profiles and hardware-specific rate rounding are not modeled or configured by this lab.
Primary Cisco IOS and IOS XE CoPP documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed; existing IOS/NX-OS CML regression contracts pass in the full suite.
No theme/layout, terminal styling, node artwork, dependency or backend/server changes.
